title: The Underhanded C Contest
summary: The Underhanded C Contest is an annual programming competition where participants write C code that appears legitimate and passes normal review but contains hidden malicious functionality. The contest challenges programmers to create subtle, hard-to-detect vulnerabilities that look like innocent bugs.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of understanding how covert vulnerabilities can be hidden in seemingly innocent code, helping security researchers improve their code auditing skills.
why_valuable: This contest provides hands-on training in detecting subtle vulnerabilities and understanding attacker's mindset, which is crucial for writing secure code and conducting effective security reviews.
